modules.name: Growth Strategy
modules.framework: Bain Full Potential — where to play / how to win

findings.Red: No explicit growth thesis. Activity is being mistaken for strategy.
findings.Yellow: A growth intent exists, but it is not sequenced against a binding constraint.
findings.Green: The core growth thesis is clear enough to allocate capital and attention.

modules.name: Market Positioning
modules.framework: Bain Founder's Mentality / relative win rate

findings.Red: Win rate and offer clarity are not defending share.
findings.Yellow: Positioning is uneven — some segments win, the rest leak.
findings.Green: The company knows where it wins and can say why.

modules.name: Pricing Strategy
modules.framework: Bain / McKinsey pricing waterfall and pockets of growth

findings.Red: Discounting and mix are destroying contribution after the sale.
findings.Yellow: Price architecture exists but is not enforced at the deal desk.
findings.Green: Pricing and mix are protecting margin while still converting.

modules.name: Sales Process Maturity
modules.framework: ISI Sales Process Maturity + Bain commercial excellence

findings.Red: Hero selling. CRM is a graveyard. Forecasts are stories.
findings.Yellow: A process exists; managers do not inspect it weekly.
findings.Green: Qualification, stages, and forecast have one definition of done.

modules.name: Pipeline Velocity
modules.framework: Bain commercial excellence — coverage, conversion, cycle

findings.Red: Coverage and cycle time cannot produce the number.
findings.Yellow: Pipeline looks large; aging and stage quality are weak.
findings.Green: Velocity is measurable and inspected, not hoped.

modules.name: Customer Segmentation
modules.framework: Bain NPS / Elements of Value — who is worth serving

findings.Red: Concentration and poor mix put the book at risk.
findings.Yellow: Some accounts are treasures; they are treated like everyone else.
findings.Green: ICP and account tiers drive pursuit, service, and price.

findings.Red: Coverage model does not match where demand actually sits.
findings.Yellow: Direct vs partner is unresolved; sellers improvise.
findings.Green: Channel choices match economics and relationship intensity.

modules.name: GTM Architecture
modules.framework: Bain Results Delivery — commercial operating system

findings.Red: GTM is a pile of tools and meetings, not a system.
findings.Yellow: Pieces of a GTM system exist; they do not connect.
findings.Green: Roles, cadence, CRM, and capacity form one commercial OS.

archetypes.name: Growth Engine Stalled
archetypes.headline: The revenue engine is not producing share. Fix the commercial system before adding cost.
archetypes.situation: Pipeline quality, win rate, and process maturity are below a repeatable growth band.
archetypes.implication: Hiring more sellers or spending more on demand will amplify noise, not bookings.
archetypes.recommendation: Install commercial excellence: qualification, velocity, pricing pockets, and a weekly inspect cadence.
rootCause: Win rate and pipeline quality cannot defend or grow share
Commercial process is not a managed system
Pricing and mix are leaking after the handshake
Coverage is not matched to the ICP

archetypes.name: Constrained Growth
archetypes.headline: Growth is available in the core — it is gated by a few commercial constraints, not by ambition.
archetypes.situation: The engine is not in crisis, but it is not Green. Conversion, mix, or process is the governor.
archetypes.implication: Unfocused initiative load will stall both the number and the team.
archetypes.recommendation: Pick three commercial priorities. Sequence velocity and mix before expansion bets.
rootCause: Ambition is ahead of commercial operating-system maturity
A handful of modules are Yellow and jointly cap growth
ICP and pricing are not fully enforced
The core can grow if the binding constraint is isolated

archetypes.name: Commercial Full Potential
archetypes.headline: The core commercial engine is healthy. The question is where incremental growth is earned.
archetypes.situation: Process, velocity, and positioning are in a healthy band.
archetypes.implication: The risk is unfocused adjacency, not a broken engine.
archetypes.recommendation: Protect the core OS. Treat new streams and offices as Horizon-2 bets with gates.
rootCause: The core can fund disciplined growth
Full potential is in mix, key accounts, and where to play next
Expansion is optional, not a rescue mission
Initiative load is the main risk

initiatives.name: Pipeline Quality and Velocity Reset
initiatives.summary: Rebuild stage definitions, aging rules, and weekly pipeline inspection so coverage is real.

initiatives.name: Win-Rate Engine (Proposal to Close)
initiatives.summary: Isolate where deals die and install a win-plan standard.

initiatives.name: Pricing Pocket and Discount Discipline
initiatives.summary: Recover leaked price through list, discount, terms, and giveaways.

initiatives.name: ICP and Mix Refocus
initiatives.summary: Concentrate pursuit where win rate, margin, and cost-to-serve actually work.

initiatives.name: Forecast Integrity Cadence
initiatives.summary: Replace hopeful forecasts with commit/upside rules and a weekly commercial stand-up.

initiatives.name: CRM as System of Record
initiatives.summary: Required fields, stage exit criteria, and manager inspection.

initiatives.name: Qualification Gate before Estimating
initiatives.summary: Stop spending proposal effort on unqualified work.

initiatives.name: Seller Capacity and Territory Design
initiatives.summary: Match coverage to opportunity density. Hire only after cadence is real.

initiatives.name: Sales Cycle Compression
initiatives.summary: Remove wait states: estimating SLA, decision-maker map, proposal factory.

initiatives.name: Offer Architecture and Value Narrative
initiatives.summary: Clarify what is sold, to whom, and why it wins.

initiatives.name: Key Account Growth System
initiatives.summary: Named owner and quarterly growth plan for accounts that already pay.

initiatives.name: Partner and Channel Motion
initiatives.summary: Add a controlled partner motion only where direct coverage cannot reach economically.

initiatives.name: Core Productivity before Headcount
initiatives.summary: Squeeze qualified meetings and proposals from the current team before adding cost.

initiatives.name: Referral and Proof Engine
initiatives.summary: Turn delivery proof into a systematic referral motion.

initiatives.name: Demand System (Not Random Activity)
initiatives.summary: Replace random marketing with a measured funnel into the same ICP and CRM.

initiatives.name: Fractional BD Leadership Seat
initiatives.summary: Operator-owned commercial cadence when a full-time VP is not yet justified.

initiatives.name: Commercial Value Leak Map
initiatives.summary: Quantify leaks: price, mix, cost-to-serve, and concentration. Assign an owner to each.

initiatives.name: Margin Mix Shift
initiatives.summary: Grow work that prints contribution; reprice or sunset work that does not.
